newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU confirms no change to oilseed penalty system.
newsitem.headline: EU confirms no change to oilseed penalty system.

text.p: The European Commission confirmed that increased profitability for cereals had led to a decline in European Union oilseeds planting.
This meant that plantings in the 1996/97 marketing year would not exceed the maximum guaranteed area (MGA) of 4.93 million hectares set under the Blair House agreement in 1992.
EU oilseed growers would not suffer penalty deductions on their oilseed compensatory payments and no change to the penalty system was needed, the Commission said in a report.

The report to the Council and the European Parliament said national measures had reduced the risk of overplanting together with "...a move to cereals caused by the level of market prices, the dissuasive effect of penalties applied in 1994/95 and the risk that penalties would be maintained for the following market year if the MGA were again to be exceeded."

Penalties would not apply despite the fact that Spain, France, Finland and the UK would have exceeded their MGAs in 1995/96 and again in 1996/97 because penalties are triggered only if the EU as a whole exceeds its MGA.
The Commission confirmed in the report that because of the overall undershoot in oilseed plantings it did not intend to change the method of application of the panalties system.
